trail update: validate every input before touching the forge

`entire trail update --trail N --set-branch b --branch-action create
--title ""` created the branch on the forge and only then failed on the
empty title, leaving a branch behind that nothing rolls back. The branch
work ran first because applyTrailBranchChange both decided what
--set-branch meant and carried it out, and it was called well before
validateTrailUpdateFields.

Split the deciding from the doing. planTrailBranchChange takes no API
client, so it cannot reach the forge: it validates the branch flags and
returns a trailBranchPlan saying whether this is a rename (folded into the
metadata PATCH) or an attach (a POST to /branch), with the trimmed branch
name and the action. attachTrailBranchPlan performs an attach, and now runs
after validateTrailUpdateFields, next to the PATCH calls that are the
update's other server-side writes.

An invalid --title, --status, --type or --priority alongside --set-branch
now fails with nothing created. Output is unchanged: the attach line still
prints before "Updated trail #N".

Cover planTrailBranchChange directly — the rename, attach, default-to-link
and trimming cases, plus each input it rejects.

## Merged `origin/main`

Two conflicts, both in the trail update command, where main had grown `--add-assignee` / `--add-reviewer` / `--type` / `--priority` right next to this branch's branch flags. `TrailUpdateRequest`, `trailUpdateInputs`, `newTrailUpdateCmd`, and the no-flags check that opens the interactive form all took the union of both sets.

The one that wasn't mechanical: main replaced the single inline `client.Patch` with `splitTrailUpdate` + `sendTrailPatch`, so the branch rename had to move onto that path. That surfaced two things a plain conflict resolution would have shipped broken:

- `splitTrailUpdate`'s `hasMeta` didn't count `Branch`, so a rename-only update would have sent no PATCH at all and silently done nothing.
- The "nothing left to send" early return listed changed fields by hand, and that list had already gone stale against main's new flags — `--add-assignee` on its own would have returned early and skipped the PATCH. It now asks `splitTrailUpdate` instead of re-listing fields.

## Addressed the review finding

The finding was right: `applyTrailBranchChange` both decided what `--set-branch` meant *and* carried it out, and ran well before `validateTrailUpdateFields`. So `--set-branch b --branch-action create --title ""` created the branch on the forge, then failed on the empty title, leaving the branch behind.

Split the deciding from the doing. `planTrailBranchChange` takes no API client — it structurally cannot reach the forge — and returns a `trailBranchPlan` (rename vs attach, plus the trimmed branch and action). `attachTrailBranchPlan` does the POST, and now runs after validation, next to the PATCH calls. Output ordering is unchanged: the attach line still prints before `Updated trail #N`.

Added direct tests for `planTrailBranchChange` (rename, attach, default-to-link, trimming, and each rejected input), which also closes the coverage gap the confidence monitor called out on that helper.
